description.en: Use vision APIs to analyze images, extract text from documents, and combine text with visual understanding.
description.ta: படங்களை பகுப்பாய்வு செய்ய, ஆவணங்களிலிருந்து உரையை பிரித்தெடுக்க, உரையை visual புரிதலுடன் இணைக்க vision API-களைப் பயன்படுத்துங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Vision Lab

Vaathiyaar holds up a photograph. "Students, until recently, LLMs could only process text. Now they can SEE. GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet — they understand images, charts, screenshots, handwritten notes. This is multi-modal AI."

### What is Multi-Modal AI?

AI that processes multiple types of input:
- **Text + Image** → Describe what's in a photo
- **Text + Document** → Extract data from invoices, receipts
- **Text + Code Screenshot** → Convert screenshot to working code
- **Text + Chart** → Analyze and explain data visualizations

### Use Cases

| Input | Task | Example |
|-------|------|---------|
| Photo | Description | 'A cat sitting on a laptop' |
| Receipt | Data extraction | '{total: 450, items: [...]}' |
| Chart | Analysis | 'Sales grew 23% in Q3' |
| Screenshot | Code generation | Convert mockup to HTML |
| Handwriting | OCR | Extract handwritten text |

> **Key Insight:** Multi-modal AI turns unstructured visual data into structured, actionable information. This is transformative for document processing workflows.

animation_sequence.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()

# Vision: analyze an image
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='gpt-4o',
    messages=[{'role':'user','content': [
        {'type':'text','text':'What is in this image?'},
        {'type':'image_url','image_url':{'url':'https://example.com/photo.jpg'}}
    ]}]
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# Audio: text-to-speech
audio = client.audio.speech.create(
    model='tts-1', voice='alloy', input='Hello from PyMasters!'
)
print('Audio generated successfully')

instruction.en: Send an image plus a question to a vision model. The sandbox has no network or files, so `FakeOpenAI` stands in for the client and `read_bytes(path)` for reading a local file. 1) `image_part(image_source)`: for an http(s) URL return {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_source}}; for a local path, base64-encode `read_bytes(image_source)` and use the URL "data:image/png;base64,<encoded>". 2) `analyze_image(client, image_source, question)`: call `client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=[...])` with one user message whose content is a list: a {"type": "text", "text": question} part and the image part; return the reply text.
instruction.ta: ஒரு படத்தையும் கேள்வியையும் vision model-க்கு அனுப்புங்கள். Sandbox-ல் network-உம் files-உம் இல்லாததால், client-க்குப் பதிலாக `FakeOpenAI`-உம், local file படிப்பதற்குப் பதிலாக `read_bytes(path)`-உம் உள்ளன. 1) `image_part(image_source)`: http(s) URL என்றால் {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_source}} திருப்புங்கள்; local path என்றால் `read_bytes(image_source)`-ஐ base64 encode செய்து "data:image/png;base64,<encoded>" URL-ஐப் பயன்படுத்துங்கள். 2) `analyze_image(client, image_source, question)`: content ஒரு list ஆக உள்ள ஒரு user message உடன் `client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=[...])`-ஐ அழையுங்கள் - அதில் {"type": "text", "text": question} பகுதியும் image பகுதியும் இருக்க வேண்டும்; பதில் text-ஐத் திருப்புங்கள்.

en: For a file: encoded = base64.b64encode(read_bytes(image_source)).decode('utf-8'); url = f'data:image/png;base64,{encoded}'

practice_challenges.test_code:
import base64
_u = image_part("https://example.com/cat.jpg")
assert _u == {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/cat.jpg"}}, "a URL must be passed through as image_url.url, got " + repr(_u)
_f = image_part("chart.png")
assert isinstance(_f, dict) and _f.get("type") == "image_url", "a local file must also become an image_url part"
_url = _f["image_url"]["url"]
assert _url.startswith("data:image/png;base64,"), "a local file must become a data:image/png;base64, URL"
assert base64.b64decode(_url.split(",", 1)[1]) == read_bytes("chart.png"), "the data URL must hold the base64-encoded file bytes"
_c = FakeOpenAI()
_ans = analyze_image(_c, "chart.png", "What does this show?")
assert _ans == "Answer about the uploaded image: a bar chart with three bars.", "analyze_image must return response.choices[0].message.content"
_req = _c.chat.completions.last_request
assert _req["model"] == "gpt-4o", "use model='gpt-4o'"
_parts = _req["messages"][-1]["content"]
assert _req["messages"][-1]["role"] == "user", "send the image in a 'user' message"
assert {"type": "text", "text": "What does this show?"} in _parts, "the content list must include the question as a text part"
assert analyze_image(FakeOpenAI(), "https://example.com/x.png", "Q") == "Answer about the linked image: a bar chart with three bars.", "URL images must work too"
print("All vision tests passed!")

under_the_hood.summary: A vision-language model cuts an image into small patches, turns each patch into a vector just like a text token, and feeds those image tokens into the same transformer alongside your text so attention can relate words to regions.

steps.title: Images become patches
steps.body: In a Vision Transformer style encoder, a 224 x 224 image split into 16 x 16 pixel patches gives 14 x 14 = 196 patches. Each patch's 16 x 16 x 3 = 768 pixel values are flattened and linearly projected to a vector, with a position embedding saying where the patch came from.

props.caption: Turning one image into 196 patch tokens

steps.title: Image tokens join the text sequence
steps.body: An image encoder refines those patch vectors, and a projection maps them into the language model's embedding space. The model then sees one sequence, image tokens followed by tokens like 'What does this receipt total?', and attention lets the question's tokens look at the relevant patches.

nodes.label: project into the LLM's token space

steps.title: Bigger images cost more tokens
steps.body: More pixels means more patches and so more tokens. Providers resize large images to a maximum size and count image tokens as part of the input, so a full-resolution screenshot costs more than a thumbnail. Small text in a downscaled image may become unreadable; cropping to the region you care about helps.

steps.title: Sending images through an API
steps.body: Chat APIs accept an image as a content part next to text, either base64-encoded bytes with a media type such as image/png or, for some providers, a URL. Several images can go in one message, and their order matters when you refer to 'the first image'.

steps.title: Documents: pixels and text together
steps.body: For PDFs, systems may extract the embedded text and also render pages as images so tables and charts are visible to the model. Asking for structured output, such as JSON with vendor, date and total, turns a receipt photo into data, but numbers read from images should be validated, for example by checking that line items add up to the total.

under_the_hood.takeaway: To the model an image is just more tokens: patch vectors placed next to your words. Give it enough resolution where details matter, keep images as small as the task allows, and verify any numbers it reads.
